name: Marcus Westberg

story_summary: Award-winning Swedish conservation photographer Marcus Westberg was on assignment in South Sudan for three weeks in 2025, documenting the movement of six million antelope — the world's largest land mammal migration — for National Geographic. He captured the first-ever drone footage of the migration. Westberg and his team used an Insta360 camera in the field during the assignment, and had to hide in the grass so that they would not be visible in the panoramic 360 frame.

name: Carlos Rigo Belliver
story_summary: Cinematographer Carlos Rigo Belliver used an Insta360 camera as a deliberate aesthetic choice alongside a RED Komodo (primary camera) and iPhone on Magic Farm (2025), a feature film written and directed by artist Amalia Ulman, starring Chloe Sevigny and Alex Wolff. The film world-premiered at the 2025 Sundance Film Festival (January 28, 2025) and screened at the 75th Berlinale (February 2025). Belliver chose the multi-format approach — incorporating Insta360 and iPhone alongside cinema cameras — to create a visual language that balanced TikTok/social media aesthetic with cinematic scope, reflecting the film's satire of influencer culture. The film went on UK general release in May 2025.

name: Ciaron Craig & Ronan Corrigan
story_summary: Director Ronan Corrigan and cinematographer Ciaron Craig deliberately used Insta360 as one of 18 cameras across 12 different formats while shooting LifeHack (2025), a screenlife thriller about Gen Z hackers. The film premiered at SXSW 2025 (March 2025) to a 100% Rotten Tomatoes critics score and opened in UK Vue cinemas in May 2026.
